source.bfsMunicipalityList: internal register data/raw/bfs_municipalities_register.csv (already present in this project, filtered to cantonCode=LU)

notes: YEAR: 2026 figures used throughout. The ESTV Kantonsblatt Luzern's income-tax bracket rows are explicitly footnoted '* Gültig für Steuerperiode 2026' (kalte-Progression / cold-progression indexation per Paragraph 61 StG, applied every year to the Landesindex der Konsumentenpreise as of 30 June before the tax period, with no minimum-CPI-move threshold unlike Bern's 3% trigger), and the canton's own official 'Steuereinheiten 2026' publication (Dienststelle Steuern, downloaded 2026-09-08) is explicitly the 2026 edition and states the cantonal Staatssteuer is 1.45 Einheiten for 2026 (DOWN from 1.55 in 2025 - a genuine, confirmed cantonal tax cut effective 2026, corroborated independently by contemporaneous news coverage, e.g. Luzerner Zeitung 'Steuern Luzern 2026: Anpassung der Tarife und Abzüge'). SOURCES SAVED: data/raw/sources/LU_kantonsblatt_estv_2026.pdf (ESTV Kantonsblatt with Paragraph 57/60 StG tariff excerpts), LU_steuereinheiten_2026_NP.pdf (official 2-page canton publication, the PRIMARY source for the municipal multiplier + church tax table used below), LU_steuereinheiten_2026_JP.pdf and LU_steuereinheiten_2026_Rangfolge.pdf (legal-persons and canton-wide ranking variants of the same publication, downloaded for completeness though not used for this natural-persons dataset), and LU_gemeindeuebersicht_2026.html (the canton's own web page rendering of the same NP table, cross-checked against the PDF). MECHANISM - 'STEUER JE EINHEIT' / STEUEREINHEITEN (structurally almost identical to Bern's Steueranlage system, a genuine LU-specific quirk worth flagging): Paragraph 57 StG's income-tax bracket table and Paragraph 60 StG's wealth-tax rate are both defined directly as the 'Steuer je Einheit' (tax PER UNIT), i.e. the bracket-table percentages/per-mille rate ARE the marginal-rate-per-unit result (this project's incomeTaxBrackets/wealthTaxBrackets above), and on top of that base result, the canton, the Einwohnergemeinde (resident municipality), and the Kirchgemeinde (parish, only if affiliated) EACH independently set their own annual multiplicative factor in 'Einheiten oder Bruchteilen von Einheiten' (units or fractions of units, e.g. municipal Luzern-city=1.45, cantonal=1.45 for 2026) per Paragraph 2 and Paragraph 236 StG; all three factors sum and multiply the same base (not chained/compounded). Exactly like this project's precedent for factor-based cantons (Bern, Graubünden), all Einheiten values here were converted to percent by multiplying by 100 for the JSON output (cantonalMultiplier.value=145 <=> the official 1.45 Einheiten; a municipality's municipalMultiplier=230 <=> 2.30 Einheiten, etc.). QUIRK - WEALTH TAX HAS NO BRACKET TABLE AT ALL (important, verified directly from Paragraph 60 StG: 'Die Steuer vom Vermögen beträgt für ein Steuerjahr 0,75 Promille je Einheit'): unlike almost every other canton modeled in this project, Lucerne's wealth tax is a completely FLAT, non-progressive per-mille rate with no thresholds or marginal steps whatsoever - a single uniform 0.75 per-mille (0.00075 decimal) applies to the entire taxable wealth above the personal deduction (see below), with only a de-minimis rounding rule (amounts under CHF 1'000 disregarded). wealthTaxBrackets.general therefore correctly contains just ONE row ({from:0, rate:0.00075}) rather than a genuine progressive schedule - this is the flattest wealth-tax mechanism among the cantons modeled so far in this project and a developer must not assume a multi-row table is missing/incomplete. There is only one unified wealth-tax rate for all filers (no separate married schedule; Paragraph 60 StG applies identically regardless of marital status - the marital distinction for wealth tax instead comes entirely through the personal deduction: Paragraph 52 StG grants a steuerfreier Betrag of CHF 125'000 for married couples living together vs CHF 62'500 for others, plus CHF 12'500 per dependent child - these deductions are NOT modeled in the bracket table itself and are out of scope of this dataset, but a developer must apply them before the flat 0.75 per-mille rate to get a correct result). MARRIED-COUPLE INCOME-TAX MECHANISM: Lucerne, like Bern, does NOT use an income-splitting divisor; Paragraph 57 Abs. 1 StG (ordinary/Grundtarif, used for single filers and other unqualified taxpayers) and Paragraph 57 Abs. 2 StG ('reduzierter Steuersatz', for married couples living together and single-parent/support-household filers) are two wholly SEPARATE, independently-legislated bracket tables with different thresholds AND different marginal rates at matching bracket positions (verified NOT to be a constant multiple of one another, ruling out a simple splitting-divisor derivation) - both tables above were transcribed directly and independently from the source's own cumulative 'X Prozent der [ersten/nächsten] Y Franken' presentation, converting each row's cumulative income into an absolute 'from' threshold paired with that row's marginal rate. QUIRK - TOP-BRACKET RATE DROP (both tariffs, genuine and verified, not a transcription error - the same phenomenon flagged in this project's SO and BE datasets): both LU tariffs rise monotonically through their printed brackets up to a peak of 5.8% marginal rate, but then the source explicitly states a LOWER flat rate applies beyond the final threshold - Grundtarif (single): 5.8% up to CHF 2'096'800, then 'bei Einkommen über 2'096'800 Franken beträgt die Steuer je Einheit 5,7 Prozent DES EINKOMMENS' (note: this is 5.7% of TOTAL income, not a marginal-only rate on the excess - functionally a proportional/flat-tax regime above this threshold rather than a continuation of progressive brackets, though this dataset models it as a marginal breakpoint at 5.7% consistent with this project's from/rate convention used for SO/BE's analogous quirk); reduzierter Tarif (married): 5.8% up to CHF 1'425'500, then flat 5.6% of income above that. Cumulative tax remains non-decreasing throughout in both tables since no rate is negative, but a naive 'rates only increase' assumption will misclassify these top-end points as bugs - they are official, deliberate features of Paragraph 57 StG. HOECHSTBELASTUNG (relief caps, Paragraph 62 StG, not modeled in the bracket tables, flagged for developers): total combined income tax (Staat + Gemeinde + Kirchgemeinde) is capped at 22.8% of taxable income under the Grundtarif or 22.4% under the reduzierter Tarif; total combined wealth tax is capped at 3.0 per-mille (0.003) of taxable wealth - both are backstop caps that only bind at very high effective combined multipliers and require knowing the taxpayer's full combined municipal+church rate to apply, out of scope here. MUNICIPAL & CHURCH DATA - CANTON-WIDE FLAT CHRIST-CATHOLIC RATE (a genuine, LU-specific quirk distinct from Bern's per-municipality christ-catholic rates): the official Steuereinheiten_2026_NP.pdf table's sixth column header is literally 'Total Einheiten inkl. Staats-, Gemeinde- und 0.31 chr. kath. Kirche' - i.e. unlike the reformed and catholic columns (which vary per municipality/Kirchgemeinde), the christ-catholic (christkatholische) church has ONE single canton-wide flat rate of 0.31 Einheiten (31%, applied on the same einheiten-multiplier basis) for the entire Kanton Luzern, reflecting that Lucerne's christ-catholic community is a single small canton-wide parish rather than multiple local Kirchgemeinden - churchMultiplierChristCatholic=31.0 was therefore populated identically for all 79 municipalities in LU_municipalities.json, sourced directly from this column header rather than per-row data (there is no per-municipality variation to report for this column). QUIRK - POOLED/SHARED KIRCHGEMEINDEN (both reformed AND catholic): many of Lucerne's 79 political municipalities do NOT have their own dedicated Kirchgemeinde; instead several municipalities share one pooled parish whose name is printed directly in the source next to the rate (e.g. Adligenswil's reformed rate of 0.25 Einheiten belongs to the pooled parish 'Meggen-Adligenswil-Udligenswil'; Alberswil's catholic rate of 0.29 belongs to the separately-named 'Ettiswil' Kirchgemeinde even though Alberswil itself is a distinct municipality). This dataset preserves that detail via two EXTRA fields beyond the required schema - reformedParish and catholicParish - naming the actual (possibly pooled, possibly cross-municipality) Kirchgemeinde each rate belongs to (defaulting to the municipality's own name when the source shows no separate pooled-parish name, i.e. the municipality has its own dedicated parish). A developer implementing per-taxpayer church tax should be aware that e.g. Meggen, Adligenswil and Udligenswil residents affiliated with the reformed church all pay into the same pooled Kirchgemeinde and hence nominally share one rate for that confession, even though their municipal (Einwohnergemeinde) multiplier differs (Meggen=90%, Adligenswil=185%, Udligenswil=180% for 2026). MUNICIPAL MULTIPLIER RANGE: 2026 Einwohnergemeinde multipliers range from a low of 125% (Luzern city=145%, actually the lowest overall is Meggen at 90%) up to 240% (Luthern), illustrating the very wide tax-rate dispersion within this canton's 5 Wahlkreise (Luzern-Stadt, Hochdorf, Sursee, Entlebuch, Willisau, matching this project's existing BFS register districtName values, used as-is with no renaming needed since LU's Wahlkreis structure directly matches the register). DATA COMPLETENESS: all 79 LU municipalities (matching this project's existing BFS register count of 79 exactly) were successfully extracted from the official 2-page PDF/HTML table and cross-matched to bfs_municipalities_register.csv bfsNumbers, resolving 6 name-suffix mismatches by hand (source 'Aesch' vs BFS-canonical 'Aesch (LU)', 'Eschenbach' vs 'Eschenbach (LU)', 'Hasle' vs 'Hasle (LU)', 'Hergiswil' vs 'Hergiswil bei Willisau', 'Rickenbach' vs 'Rickenbach (LU)', 'Zell' vs 'Zell (LU)' - all straightforward BFS-register disambiguation suffixes for municipalities that share a bare name with municipalities in other cantons). No nulls were needed for municipalMultiplier or either church rate for any of the 79 municipalities - the source table was complete for every row.
